record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: In federated learning, how can bias in the data-generating process be detected, mitigated, and corrected after training when data come from user interactions, client sampling, device conditions, product-design effects, and privacy constraints that limit direct bias inspection?

evidence.quote: biases in the data-generated process can be identified or mitigated

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a federated learning setting in which a global model is trained from data held locally on a population of client devices. Let the data-generating process be modeled as follows. There is a population of users indexed by a set U, and at each round t a (possibly non-uniform, availability-dependent) random subset S_t ⊆ U of clients is selected; each selected client i contributes a local dataset D_{i,t} drawn from a client-specific distribution P_i that depends on (a) user-interaction patterns (which items, prompts, or queries the user produces), (b) device and environment conditions (hardware capability, connectivity, time-zone, battery state), (c) product-design effects (UI choices, default settings, A/B-test cohort), and (d) privacy mechanisms M (e.g., local differential privacy, secure aggregation, sample- and user-level DP) that prevent the server from observing raw client data or per-client statistics. Let P* denote a target population distribution of interest, possibly differing from the mixture ∑_i w_i P_i induced by the sampling and participation process.

Define the "data-generation bias" as any divergence (in distribution, in subgroup representation, or in model performance across subgroups) between the training-induced distribution and the target P*, caused by mechanisms (a)–(d).

Develop a rigorous framework and concrete algorithms that simultaneously achieve the following objectives, subject to the privacy constraints imposed by M (so that no algorithm may access raw client data or non-privatized per-client statistics):

1. Detection. Provide a procedure that, using only outputs permitted by M (e.g., DP-aggregated statistics, secure-aggregation sums, public auxiliary data), produces a statistically valid test or estimator for the presence and magnitude of bias arising from (a)–(d), with provable false-discovery and power guarantees as a function of the privacy budget, number of clients sampled, and rounds.

2. Mitigation during training. Design a federated training algorithm (modification of the optimization, sampling, reweighting, or local objective) that provably reduces a specified bias functional (e.g., disparity in subgroup risk, or KL divergence between induced and target distribution) while preserving (ε, δ)-differential privacy and convergence to a stationary point of the federated objective.

3. Post-hoc correction. Given an already-trained model θ and only privacy-preserving access to client data, give a procedure that outputs a corrected model θ' with quantifiable bounds on residual bias relative to P*, again under the privacy constraints.

Prove, for each of (1)–(3), upper and matching lower bounds on the achievable bias-reduction as a function of: the privacy parameters (ε, δ), the client-sampling distribution, the amount of available public/auxiliary data, and the structural assumptions made on P_i and on the mechanisms (a)–(d). In particular, determine whether nontrivial detection, mitigation, and correction are simultaneously possible under user-level differential privacy together with secure aggregation, or establish an impossibility result.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a broad open research direction articulated as part of a list of open problems in federated learning. No comprehensive solution exists; partial progress has been made on fairness-aware federated optimization (e.g., q-FFL, AgnosticFL), DP-compatible debiasing, and group-fair federated learning, but full detection/mitigation/post-hoc correction under privacy constraints with matching guarantees remains unresolved as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Lists bias in data-generating processes, identification and mitigation under privacy constraints, as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open problem in the federated learning research agenda.

status_evidence.title: Fair Resource Allocation in Federated Learning (q-FFL)
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a fairness-aware federated objective addressing disparities across clients, but does not resolve general bias detection under privacy.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists on mitigation but not on the full detection/mitigation/correction problem.

status_evidence.title: Agnostic Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Minimax framework for federated learning over mixtures of client distributions to address representational bias.
status_evidence.claim: Mitigation has been partially addressed; detection and post-hoc correction under DP remain open.
